text:
The European Court of Human Rights in Al-Adsani v. the United Kingdom (Grand Chamber, 21 November 2001) held that immunity trumped the right of access to a court: the United Kingdom did not violate the Convention by upholding Kuwait’s state immunity and refusing Al-Adsani’s civil claim for alleged torture. It found no violation of Article 6 § 1 by nine votes to eight, treating that immunity as a proportionate limit under a generally recognised rule of international law, and no violation of Article 3 unanimously.

CONFIDENCE: 90
